cites: 01rabbit/Azazel:docs/roadmaps/service-objective-assignments.md SO-04 sample rule (leases expiring under hostile load), OF-06 and SO-11 (shed at 120% of the declared quota); 01rabbit/Azazel-Edge#414; Edge#412 (the Rust azazel-edge-core is the enforcement authority, so the load is offered to it)
note: PROVISIONAL. The hostile load SO-04 samples are taken under. Every rate below is derived from config/service_objectives/ingress_quota.json (OF-06) by the rules in this file; declarations.load_hostile_load_profile() recomputes each one and refuses the profile if any differs, so a change to the quota makes this file invalid until it is re-derived. The factors under owner_defaults are defaults chosen when the profile was written and await the owner's confirmation. Container numbers are not hardware evidence. Read only by the SO-04 harness and the validator; the core never reads it, and nothing here changes how the core reads, sheds or decides.

owner_defaults.why: non_alert_factor 1.2 is SO-11's overload point (120% of the quota) applied to OF-06's only quota. flood_alert_poll_fill 1.0 offers exactly one full alerts_per_poll budget per default poll interval, the poll cap. background_alert_poll_fill 0.2 keeps alerts flowing beside the non-alert and malformed loads so that any alert loss would show there too. oversized_line_factor 2.0 makes each oversized line twice max_line_bytes; oversized_backlog_share 0.25 holds the oversized bytes to a quarter of backlog_bound_bytes per second, so the oversized lines alone never cross the backlog bound. backlog_non_alert_factor 12 (over 10 times the quota) written once per backlog_burst_interval_ms puts more than twice backlog_bound_bytes of unread non-alert lines in front of the core at once, so its backlog shedding (shed_by_reason.backlog, max_shed_level) must act, not only the bucket.

rules.non_alert: rates_per_s summed over non_alert_kinds = round(quota.value * non_alert_factor), split equally over non_alert_kinds (each share must be a whole number). invalid_utf8 is a non-alert kind: the core classes it unparseable and draws it from the same bucket.
rules.alert: rates_per_s.alert = round(alert_poll_fill * quota.alerts_per_poll * 1000 / core_default_poll_ms): alert_poll_fill 1.0 fills one poll's alert budget every default poll interval (rust/azazel-edge-core/src/main.rs AZAZEL_EVE_POLL_MS default).
rules.oversized: oversized_line_bytes = round(oversized_line_factor * quota.max_line_bytes) and must exceed max_line_bytes; rates_per_s.oversized = oversized_backlog_share * quota.backlog_bound_bytes / oversized_line_bytes. Oversized lines are non-alert lines (no alert marker), so oversized_possible_alerts must stay 0.
rules.warmup: warmup_ms >= 1000 * quota.non_alert_burst / (non-alert rate - quota.value) for every phase over the quota: the bucket is empty, and shedding steady, before the phase's first lease expires.
rules.attribution: an ingress_shed summary belongs to the phase whose window started last before its emitted_epoch, up to the next phase's window start; the last phase keeps every later summary, including those the core emits while the harness waits for it to decide every alert written (alerts are written last in every chunk, so that wait covers every line). The backlog phase must be the last phase, because the core may still be reading its backlog after the window. audit_attribution_slack_ms >= quota.audit_interval_ms and quiet_gap_ms > audit_attribution_slack_ms.
rules.line_bytes: every non-oversized line is padded to about line_bytes, as the SO-11 probe does (so11_ingress_probe.LINE_BYTES).
rules.burst: burst_interval_ms 0 writes continuously (every 10 ms). Otherwise every class of the phase is written in one burst per burst_interval_ms; a phase whose burst of non-alert bytes (rate * burst_interval_ms / 1000 * line_bytes) is at least twice backlog_bound_bytes is a backlog phase, and the core must record backlog shedding (shed_by_reason.backlog >= 1 and max_shed_level >= 1) in it. The profile must have one backlog phase with non_alert_factor over 10.
rules.shed: for every phase over the quota: every summary adds up (examined = shed_total + admitted + oversized_lines_skipped); the summaries attributed to the phase account for at least (1 - shed_tolerance) of the non-alert lines written in it (examined minus alerts_admitted, so that alerts of another phase read late do not count); the lines shed are at least max(1, (1 - shed_tolerance) * (non-alert written - quota.value * read_s - quota.non_alert_burst)); and the non-alert lines admitted are at most quota.value * read_s + quota.non_alert_burst.
rules.samples: each declared phase gets leases_per_phase_per_action leases of every action type and nominal takes the rest of SO-04's 50 per type (4 phases * 10 = 40 of 50); the validator requires at least leases_per_phase_per_action per phase and action type, and at least min_hostile_share of all samples under a declared phase.
rules.confirmation: status confirmed is accepted only with owner_defaults.status exactly 'confirmed' and owner_defaults.confirmed_phase_factors equal to every phase's factors (non_alert_factor, alert_poll_fill, oversized_line_factor, oversized_backlog_share, burst_interval_ms) as they stand, so a confirmation names the values it confirmed.
rules.read: read_s, the time a phase's lines could have been admitted. Outside the backlog phase the core keeps up (peak unread backlog under 4 MB in every run, read within one poll), so its reading ends within read_lag_cap_ms of the window: read_s = window + read_lag_cap_ms, fixed, whenever its summaries are emitted (a summary is due at most one audit interval after the shedding it reports, so its emission time says when it was written, not when the lines were read). read_lag_cap_ms lies between one poll interval and the audit interval; 1000 ms is the audit interval, five times the poll interval and the time to read the largest unread backlog seen. In the backlog phase the core may read long after the window: read_s runs from the window start to the last summary attributed to the phase, at least the window and at most window + backlog_read_lag_cap_ms (60000 ms: the largest lag seen, about 12 s from the window end to its last summary on a GitHub runner, five times over, and within the harness's 90000 ms drain); summaries emitted after that cap are not counted as shed. Even at the cap the floor stays near 61000 lines, while honest records shed more than 170000.

phases.name: non_alert_flood
phases.derivation: non-alert 2500 * 1.2 = 3000 lines/s over 4 kinds (750 each), above the 2500/s quota, so the core must shed; alerts 0.2 * 1000 * 1000 / 200 = 1000/s, none of which may be shed.

phases.name: malformed_mix
phases.derivation: non-alert 2500 * 1.2 = 3000 lines/s over 5 kinds including invalid UTF-8 (600 each); oversized lines of 2 * 1 MiB at 0.25 * 8 MiB / 2 MiB = 1 line/s, every one of which the core must skip and count; alerts 1000/s as above.

phases.name: alert_flood
phases.derivation: alerts 1.0 * 1000 * 1000 / 200 = 5000/s: one full alerts_per_poll budget per default poll interval, the poll cap; alerts are outside the quota and must all be decided.

phases.name: backlog_flood
phases.derivation: non-alert 2500 * 12 = 30000 lines/s over 4 kinds (7500 each), written in one burst per second: about 30000 * 600 = 18 MB, more than twice the 8 MiB backlog bound, so the core sheds by backlog as well as by rate; alerts 1000/s as above, none of which may be shed.
